approach: Re-planned against the spec's last revision: DEDL splits into DISL (.disl, what a tool engineer specifies) and DID (.did, how users' diagrams are stored), with DESL/DED and EDSL/EDD as placeholders. Every language uses its lowercase acronym as <name> and extension; DEDL is retired, its old identifiers read or redirected as DISL/DID. Seven parallel parts coordinated by the glossary, classification, rename map and terminology check.

decisions.decision: Retire DEDL entirely: remove specifications/dedl/, redirect /adp/dedl/ to DISL, and never reuse DEDL identifiers
decisions.why: Peter renamed the definition languages to DID, DED and EDD, so the acronym is no longer needed and the redirect conflict disappears
decisions.rejected: Reusing specifications/dedl/ for the Designer Definition Language placeholder (previous revision)

decisions.decision: Each language uses its lowercase acronym for folder, schema, $id, media type, version key and extension (disl, did, desl, ded, edsl, edd)
decisions.why: One pattern for all six (FR-006a) and the constitution’s specifications/<name>/ rule
decisions.rejected: Keeping didl/eddl-style folder names alongside .did/.edd extensions

decisions.decision: Match acronyms case-sensitively in the terminology check and leave the W3C DID untouched
decisions.why: DID collides with the English word did and with W3C Decentralized Identifiers; third-party names are never changed
decisions.rejected: Case-insensitive matching of all retired patterns

plan.summary: Plan revised to DISL/DID, DESL/DED, EDSL/EDD with DEDL retired; research, data model, contracts and quickstart updated; no clarifications left
